searchText: I have a noob question about the functionality of Geth. How does a completely new node (that is, not initially knowing any other nodes on the network) know the IP address of the first node to connect to? Go-ethereum is shipped with a configuration that includes "bootstrap nodes". These are the initial nodes you connect to to get peers from. You can change them or add more if you don't trust the built-in bootstrap nodes. Thank you 🙂 I have a noobie question.. I know bitcoin has an algorithm that even transactions that didn't pay any fees are eventually included in a block. The longer you wait, the higher the priority for your tx. Does ethereum have anything similar? If I send a simple approve/unapprove tx with 1 gwei, will it eventually be included in a block even if the gas doesn't actually drop to 1? Nope. Only transactions that have a maxFeePerGas >= baseFeePerGas can be included. Oversimplifying a little, there's less chance overpaying with EIP-1559 but also less chance of getting a lowball offer in. excerpts.author: void.xyz
excerpts.content: I have a noob question about the functionality of Geth. How does a completely new node (that is, not initially knowing any other nodes on the network) know the IP address of the first node to connect to?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Go-ethereum is shipped with a configuration that includes "bootstrap nodes".  These are the initial nodes you connect to to get peers from.  You can change them or add more if you don't trust the built-in bootstrap nodes.

excerpts.author: sandreckoner
excerpts.content:
I have a noobie question.. I know bitcoin has an algorithm that even transactions that didn't pay any fees are eventually included in a block. The longer you wait, the higher the priority for your tx.
Does ethereum have anything similar? If I send a simple approve/unapprove tx with 1 gwei, will it eventually be included in a block even if the gas doesn't actually drop to 1?

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: Nope. Only transactions that have a maxFeePerGas >= baseFeePerGas can be included. Oversimplifying a little, there's less chance overpaying with EIP-1559 but also less chance of getting a lowball offer in.

excerpts.author: treyzania
excerpts.content: This is completely out of a miner's own altruism though, the game-theoretically optimal tx inclusion strategy does not do this
